notes.ttakisi: A shared minibus that runs a fixed route.
notes.siteegi: Where taxis and boda bodas wait.
notes.egenda: For n- nouns: ttakisi egenda, the taxi goes.
notes.ennyonyi: Not a bird! A bird is ekinyonyi.

guidebook.intro: Travel in Uganda means shared taxis, long-distance buses and boda bodas. Knowing a few words makes every journey easier.

tips.title: Taxi, stage and park
body: A **ttakisi** is a shared minibus that runs a fixed route from a **paaka** (taxi park). Along the way it stops at a **siteegi** (stage). Tell the conductor **Yimirira wano** when you want to get off.

tips.title: From … to …
body: Use **okuva** (from) and **okutuuka** (until, up to) for a journey: **Okuva e Kampala okutuuka e Jinja**.
Before a town name, Luganda often adds **e**: **e Kampala**, **e Masaka**. It works like “at” or “to” for places.

culture.title: Safe arrival
body: When someone arrives from a journey, people say **Kulika olugendo** (well done for the journey). The traveller answers **Weebale**. Calling to say **Ntuuse** (I’ve arrived) is a kindness.
